description: Make backup protection honest by distinguishing local-only app backups from off-host disaster-recovery backups and adding the first supported off-host destination path with retention visibility.

timing.plannedEarliestExecution: After admin auth and before setup wizard is considered launch-complete
timing.gatingCondition: Requires choosing the first supported off-host destination strategy and how credentials are stored/masked.

principles: Local backup is not disaster recovery
The UI must not imply same-VM backups protect against VM or disk loss
Start with one boring off-host destination before generic backup plugins
Restore proof matters as much as backup creation
Backup destination secrets must be masked and auditable

techStack.runtime: existing backup planner plus off-host sync command such as rsync/scp or mounted path copy
techStack.storage: SQLite backup records plus backup destination config and retention metadata
techStack.testing: Planner tests, dry-run tests, manual VM backup to off-host target and restore rehearsal

userStories.title: Homebase identifies local-only backup risk
acceptanceCriteria: Dashboard/app cards indicate when backups are stored only under the VM/local backup root
Local-only state is displayed as a launch-confidence warning
Backup records include destination class: local, off_host, unknown
Docs and UI explain what local backup protects and does not protect
userStories.testStrategy: State/record tests plus manual browser verification on default VM config

userStories.title: Founder can configure one off-host backup destination
acceptanceCriteria: Settings supports one first-class destination option with clear prerequisites
Destination config is validated before use
Backup execution can copy or sync completed backup artifacts to the destination
userStories.testStrategy: Planner and config validation tests plus manual off-host sync test

userStories.title: Retention and restore confidence are visible
acceptanceCriteria: Homebase shows latest local and off-host backup timestamps per app
Retention policy is explicit even if simple
Restore picker can identify whether a backup is local-only or off-host replicated
A manual restore rehearsal can prove the off-host artifact is usable
userStories.testStrategy: SQLite record tests plus manual VM restore from replicated artifact

high: A failed off-host sync can create false confidence if local backup still succeeded
Credential handling for remote destinations can become a security liability
medium: Generic backup destinations can sprawl; first version must stay narrow
Large backups may make synchronous job logs noisy or slow
low: Existing backup artifact layout can remain the source of truth

preFlightChecklist: Choose first off-host destination: mounted path, rsync over SSH, or external drive path
Define destination config validation and masking
Define whether off-host sync is part of backup job or separate replication job
